Selection barriers

Why mixing counsellors and medical doctors creates harmful recommendations

Psychological counselling and medical psychotherapy have distinct professional and regulatory considerations. AI may incorrectly attribute medical credentials, diagnoses or guaranteed treatment outcomes.

01

Professional role is ambiguous

The public label 'psychotherapist' requires clarification of qualifications and service scope. Medical psychotherapists have specific healthcare qualification requirements; counselling psychologists must be represented accurately.

02

Promises resemble medical claims

Statements such as 'cure depression in five sessions' need clinical evidence and proper authority. Search-oriented text should not present unsupported individual treatment guarantees.

03

Testimonials expose sensitive information

Client narratives, conversations and health details require strong privacy protection and lawful permission. Testimonials do not replace evidence of training and practice scope.

Verifiable facts

Evidence behind a credible practitioner profile

Russian Ministry of Labour Standard 537n concerns psychological counselling, while Ministry of Health Order 206n sets medical qualification requirements including psychotherapy. Regulated medical activity requires the applicable licensing checks, alongside careful handling of personal information.

  • Education, specialisation, accurate role titles and the actual service provided
  • Any applicable medical licence, verified address or online format, appointments, fees and terms
  • Consent and lawful handling of sensitive details, confidentiality and permissible professional publications

Standards and registers do not rank clinical quality. No patient diagnoses, testimonials or measured GAEO client outcomes in private counselling are asserted.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Are psychologists and medical psychotherapists the same for GEO?+

No. They are distinct professional roles. Accurately identify qualifications, regulated medical status where relevant and actual services.

Can I promise results after a fixed number of sessions?+

A fixed outcome is not generally supportable. Describe the professional process and limitations without universal therapeutic guarantees.

Does a private psychologist need a medical licence?+

It depends on the activity actually offered. Medical services have licensing requirements, while non-medical counselling should be assessed on its own legal and professional basis.

Can client experiences be published as case studies?+

Private and health-related information requires lawful grounds and careful consent. General anonymised professional explanations are often more appropriate.

What does GAEO charge counselling practices?+

Published GAEO plans apply. Scope depends on genuine practice areas, formats, regions and the baseline prompt matrix.
